verdictStatement.summary: The central claim (EP9-NEG-EP8-MINTS-AUTHORITY-OVER-SECOND-DIGEST) is REAL and, if anything, understated: I reproduced it from scratch without reading the author's probe, and it moves far more than the receipt digest. The re-pin machinery, the measured-count discipline, the live --selftest and the 0/1/2/3 exit matrix are all genuine and survived every attack I made on them. v9 is rejected on two published claims that I falsified constructively: (1) RES-EP9-05's load-bearing mitigation that the type-level false-accept class 'moves NO proof identity because every ref is derived from the stored raw CAS bytes' is false — I moved three durable identities under a byte-identical EvaluationAuthoritySealRef — and the 'exact admitted set' it enumerates is an artifact of v9's single-position injection regime, over-stating two sites and omitting two identity-moving ones; and (2) astScanScope.isSoleGuard=false is false — I built one evasion caught ONLY by the syntactic scan and a second that satisfies the scan's own routing rule, keeps the non-AST liveness counter ticking, and still binds every real PlanIntent's authority to the DEFECTIVE check-c2.py bytes while check-evaluation-proof-v9.py exits 0 with the full green 'C-2 join RE-PINNED' banner.

blockers.title: RES-EP9-05's identity-inertness mitigation is false, and the 'exact admitted set' is an artifact of the injection regime, not the class
blockers.statement: evaluation-proof.v9.json knownLimitations[RES-EP9-05] and scalarLeafTotality.surfaces[evaluation-authority-candidate].admittedPositionsNote assert: 'On the frozen bytes this moves NO proof identity: every RawCasRef, the EvaluationAuthoritySealRef and the admission ref are derived from the stored raw CAS bytes rather than from the in-memory record.' The stated REASON is factually wrong: check-evaluation-proof-v8.py line 480 computes admission_ref = ep6.raw_record_ref('EvaluationAuthorityAdmissionV1', admission) from the IN-MEMORY record, and that value is written into the durable EvaluationAuthorityIndexV1 row and into the index fingerprint. The conclusion is therefore true only under v9's own census regime, which injects at ONE in-memory position and leaves the stored CAS bytes at the honest encoding. Acting as a self-consistent PRODUCER instead — emitting the record and its canonical bytes together, exactly as an honest producer does — a JSON true at planAuthorityReceipt.schemaVersion is ADMITTED by EP8's public authorize_evaluation and MOVES three durable identities (receipt CAS ref, admission ref, index fingerprint) beneath a byte-identical EvaluationAuthoritySealRef; the resulting store cold-reconstructs through resolve_stored_evaluation with planAuthorityReceipt.schemaVersion = JSON true and assert_store_continuity() returning True. The same holds for admittedResolvedInputs.schemaVersion and for evaluationAuthorityAdmission.schemaVersion — TWO SITES v9 DOES NOT LIST. Conversely two of the four sites v9 does list (activationManifest.schemaVersion, evaluationAuthoritySeal.schemaVersion) are REJECTED under producer consistency by the EP5 semantic encoder's canonical-unsigned-decimal guard, so they are inert. The published set both over-states and under-states the class it claims to enumerate exactly, and 'makes any change to that set a finding' therefore pins the wrong set. This is the corpus's own dominant failure mode — a coverage claim quantified over a region the instrument cannot observe — reappearing inside the repair that exists to prevent it.

blockers.title: astScanScope.isSoleGuard=false is falsified: the syntactic scan is the sole guard for the C-2 join binding outside a fixed 8-case probe family
blockers.statement: evaluation-proof.v9.json astScanScope declares isSoleGuard=false and names 'the LB-C2-01 behavioural battery and the Authority.c2v4 access counter, neither of which reads source' as the load-bearing guard; repairs[REP-EP9-5] says 'The scan is declared a tripwire, never the guard ... the independent behavioural layer ... is required to catch every one.' I falsified this constructively with two reviewer-authored evasions that are not among the author's nine. EVASION R1 (route the LB-C2-01 probe family to the repaired module, everything else to the superseded module) was caught by EXACTLY ONE finding — EP9-SCAN, the syntactic scan — and by nothing else: not by the LB-C2-01 battery, not by the c2v4 access counter, not by the evasion battery, not by the plan-intent surface census. For that evasion the AST scan WAS the sole guard, which is the stated blocker condition. EVASION R4 then repaired R1's only tell: every C-2 reference is an ast.Attribute on an Authority accessor Call, so the scan is silent BY ITS OWN RULES; authority.c2v4() is touched on every path so c2v4_accesses still increments; and the probe family still reaches the repaired instrument so the battery, the evasion battery and the surface census all see repaired answers. check-evaluation-proof-v9.py then exits 0 and prints the complete green banner including 'C-2 join RE-PINNED onto c2-plan-stage-schema.v4.json / check-c2-v4.py' and 'LB-C2-01 battery: ... repaired join admitted 0' — while 100% of the seven pinned vectors' validate_plan_intent calls are served by the SUPERSEDED check-c2.py bytes (instrumented call counter: {v3: 1, v4: 0}). The instrument cannot distinguish 'the join was re-pinned onto C-2 v4' from 'the join is still on C-2 v3 with an eight-case whitelist', which is the entire substance of REP-EP9-1.

centralClaimAdjudication.finding: REAL. Independently reproduced from scratch without reading the author's probe.
centralClaimAdjudication.isItReal: Yes. Executing the frozen bytes of check-evaluation-proof-v8.py, its module-level public authorize_evaluation(store, candidate) ADMITS a candidate whose admittedResolvedInputs.frozenPlanIntent.schemaVersion is JSON true and mints a complete _AdmittedEvaluationAuthorityV1 whose PlanAuthorityReceiptV1 carries sha256:5d748405d6d02ad460c54b078edfd6a627d6bd5273c41e7ba5febdd6153020d9 in place of the true sha256:7c3174f6358f40a36f19b97eab6b247086f7a5411141fb9ee056535904fa7a85. check-c2-v4.py rejects that same PlanIntent with ('C2I-02', 'PlanIntent schemaVersion must be the JSON integer 1; got boolean True').
centralClaimAdjudication.isItAPrivatePathOrHandBuiltCandidate: No. I did not hand-build a candidate: I acted as a PRODUCER. I took the accepted EP8-POS-NOMATCH-PASS vector, changed one wire value, and then recomputed every derived field — commitment, planId, receipt, activation manifest, seal, admission, all three raw CAS rows and their bytes, both semantic rows and bindings, and the full dependency-edge set — using the pinned encoders exactly as an honest producer must. The result is a candidate the real pipeline WOULD produce if it accepted the value, and EP8 admitted it end to end. The only private symbol I used was _open_test_project_store, which mints the TRUSTED store capability; that is not the attack surface. The store I supplied was legitimate, freshly opened and EMPTY, and had never seen candidate JSON. The hostile input was solely the caller-supplied candidate, which is precisely the untrusted payload authorize_evaluation exists to validate.
centralClaimAdjudication.isAuthorizeEvaluationPubliclyReachable: Yes as an entrypoint: authorize_evaluation(store, candidate) is a module-level function with no leading underscore, and the candidate is wholly caller-supplied. The store capability is token-guarded and, inside this checker-scope artifact, obtainable only via the private _open_test_project_store test double (open_project_store_authority requires _HostProjectAdmissionV1 and _TrustedStoreState, neither of which has a public constructor). In a real host the store would be host-minted, so a real consumer holding a legitimate store hits exactly this path. Scoped honestly: this is checker-scope evidence about a specified contract, not a demonstration against a production store — which v9 itself states in knownLimitations[0].
centralClaimAdjudication.isTheTrueDigestWhatV9Says: Yes, verified independently and redundantly. plan_intent_commitment over the unmutated intent returns sha256:7c3174f6358f40a36f19b97eab6b247086f7a5411141fb9ee056535904fa7a85 under BOTH check-c2.py and check-c2-v4.py, with byte-identical 2463-byte canonical preimages, and that is the value evaluation-proof.v8.json itself carries.
centralClaimAdjudication.rootCause: The `!= 1` equivalence class, and nothing else. check-c2.py line 555 `if intent.get("schemaVersion") != 1:` and line 342 `if value["schemaVersion"] != 1:` are bare inequalities against the integer 1 in a language where True == 1 and 1.0 == 1. I confirmed the full truth table directly against the frozen bytes: JSON true -> ADMITTED, commits to a SECOND digest; JSON 1.0 -> ADMITTED, then raises ValueError('floating-point values are forbidden') inside the encoder; JSON false, JSON "1", JSON 0 and JSON 2 -> correctly rejected with C2I-02, because those are not == 1. The class is exactly {values v with v == 1 but v is not the JSON integer 1}. check-c2-v4.py repairs it with exact-type predicates and names the offending type in the message.
centralClaimAdjudication.isTheAuthorOverstatingIt: No — the author UNDERSTATES it. v9 reports the effect as 'a PlanAuthorityReceiptV1 carrying the second commitment'. In fact the entire minted authority moves: planId (plan1:sha256:1fc7a400... vs plan1:sha256:0c0604a8...), the ActivationManifestV1 and EvaluationAuthoritySealV1 executionPlanCommitment, the EvaluationAuthoritySealRef itself (sha256:e369f6fa... vs sha256:63172661...), the admission ref, and the durable EvaluationAuthorityIndexV1 fingerprint. A PASSED surface therefore mints a complete, durable, cold-reconstructible authority over a wrong plan identity, not merely a wrong digest field.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: OVERSTATED. All seven positiveVectors carry ONE distinct frozenPlanIntent and ONE distinct planDescriptor (verified by canonical-JSON digest: all seven hash to e4542152b262e324...). planIntentCommitmentStability publishes vectors=7 / recomputedUnderV4=7 / reproducedUnderSupersededEncoder=7 / preimageByteIdentical=7 / distinctCommitments=[one], and the green banner prints '7 vectors recomputed under C-2 v4, 7 reproduced under the superseded independent encoder, 7 with BYTE-IDENTICAL preimages; distinct commitments [1]'. That reads as seven independent confirmations converging on one commitment. It is one PlanIntent encoded seven times. 'distinctCommitments has length 1' carries no discriminating power whatsoever here — it is forced by the input, not established by the measurement. The candidate does disclose the underlying fact once, obliquely, in scalarLeafTotality.surfaceEnumerationBase ('every distinct value carried by the seven vectors'), so this is not concealment; but the headline number should state the distinct-intent count.

The behavioural layer's discriminating power is exactly 8 cases (2 leaves x 4 type-distinct values), and the plan-intent surface census adds only 6 more distinguishing positions, because C-2 v3 and v4 diverge nowhere else on that surface. My 2548-case differential fuzz found divergence at exactly 4 (path,value) pairs. Any adversarial or accidental rewiring that handles those positions correctly is invisible to both layers (see IR-EP9-02). The candidate should state the behavioural layer's measured discriminating cardinality, not just its pass rate.

delegationClosure.verificationRule ('no second disk read between verification and execution') is literally true of the ten executables and the superseded encoder, but the predecessors DO re-read pinned data from disk during execution: check-evaluation-proof-v6.py's admit_evaluation_authority calls load_json(HERE/'c2-plan-stage-schema.v3.json') and load_json(HERE/'fact-plane.v1.json') on every invocation. Both files are in EP6's own PINNED table and EP6 hash-verifies them via _modules() immediately before, so the re-read is itself verified and the trust order holds — but the rule as worded reads broader than what is enforced. Same for check-evaluation-proof-v8.py's _ep7(), which sha_file()-verifies then _load_module()s from disk.

closure_pin_agreement() cross-checks pin tables for 4 of the 10 closure members — EP8/EP7/EP6 (.PINNED) and check-c2-v4.py (.PINS). The other six (check-evaluation-proof.py, check-evidence.py, check-retention-custody.py, check-d9.py, check-versioning.py, check-resolved-inputs.py) expose no pin-like table at all; I loaded each and confirmed there is nothing to compare. That is not a defect — there is no table to disagree with — but delegationClosure.pinAgreementRule says 'every predecessor's own declared pin table', which reads as 10/10 rather than 4/4-of-those-that-have-one. Relatedly, five of the ten closure members are not reachable from the evaluation-proof authority path at all (check-evaluation-proof.py references only check-c2.py; the evidence/retention/d9/versioning/resolved checkers are executed but supply nothing to the join). Pinning them is conservative and harmless, but 'the delegation closure' is the wrong word for a set that includes members with no delegation edge.

Source comment inaccuracy at check-evaluation-proof-v9.py line ~538: 'The two leaves LB-C2-01 named, plus the third the C-2 v4 sweep found.' COMMITMENT_BEARING_LEAVES contains two entries, not three. The third site (Coverage.schemaVersion, check-c2-v4.py line 280) lives on the LB-C2-02 coverage surface, which the evaluation-proof join does not import, so its absence is correct — but the comment asserts it is present.

Deleting the RES-EP9-01 sentence from knownLimitations produces findings only incidentally, via the contract-root path census ('contractRoot publishes enumeratedPaths=6712; this run measured 6711'). The targeted RES-EP9-01 enforcement is on c2AuthorityRepairJoin.ep6InnerJoinResidual, a different field. A lane could shorten knownLimitations and would be caught, but by an arithmetic side effect rather than by the guard that exists for the purpose.

The EP9-SELFTEST liveness property (exactly one flag-guarded dispatch to selftest(), positioned before any findings return, exactly one main()) has NO behavioural counterpart inside the instrument — it is AST-only. It is externally verifiable and I verified it externally (distinct outputs, distinct exit codes 0/1/2/3), so I am not treating it as a blocker; but by the candidate's own standard it is a property for which the scan is the sole in-instrument guard, and astScanScope does not say so.

Unavoidable for a self-scan, and I note it only so the trust-order claim is not over-read to cover the instrument's own source.
